slides.title: Memory Overhead of Virtual Functions
slides.prompt: How does adding at least one virtual function affect the size of a class instance?
options: Increases object size by the size of one pointer (sizeof(void*))
Doubles the size of all member variables
Increases object size by the size of every virtual method body
Has zero impact on instance memory size
slides.correctAnswer: Increases object size by the size of one pointer (sizeof(void*))

slides.title: VTable Creation Timing
slides.prompt: VTables are generated by the compiler at ___ time.

slides.title: Runtime Cost of Virtual Dispatch
slides.prompt: Why is calling a virtual function slightly slower than a standard function call?
options: Requires pointer indirection (vptr -> vtable lookup -> function address)
Requires dynamic memory allocation on Heap during invocation
Forces function parameters to be copied twice
Triggers runtime type registration with operating system
slides.correctAnswer: Requires pointer indirection (vptr -> vtable lookup -> function address)

slides.title: Inlining Virtual Functions
slides.prompt: Can virtual function calls via base pointers usually be inlined by compilers at runtime?
slides.codeSnippet:
// Inlining virtual calls through base pointer is:
Difficult

slides.title: VPtr Setup Timing
slides.prompt: When is the vptr pointer inside an object updated to point to the current class vtable?
options: During constructor execution of each class in hierarchy
Upon first invocation of a virtual function
slides.correctAnswer: During constructor execution of each class in hierarchy

slides.title: Virtual Call Inside Constructor Danger
slides.prompt: Calling a virtual function inside a Base constructor invokes the ___ implementation.
slides.codeSnippet:
// Inside Base constructor, virtual call resolves to:
Base

slides.title: Devirtualization Optimization
slides.prompt: What is devirtualization in modern C++ compiler optimization?
options: Converting a virtual call into a direct static call when the target type is known at compile time
Removing all virtual tables from binary executable
Converting member functions into inline assembly code
slides.correctAnswer: Converting a virtual call into a direct static call when the target type is known at compile time
